To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
older people are not a homogenous group, that their needs and aspirations vary, and that the environment plays a key role in enabling independent living.
older people want to live independently in their own homes, but they need help with home modifications, and that they need to be connected with their community.

• Older people want to remain living independently at home for as long as possible, and the home is their preferred place of residence • The home and the local community provide a context for social engagement • The home is a place where people can be themselves, and where they can maintain their privacy and dignity.

the challenges of ageing in the community and the role that housing can play in enabling older people to live in a place of their choosing.
how the built environment can be designed to support ageing in place.
the social and physical environments of older people, and the impact of these environments on the health, well being and quality of life of older people.
